subject: CJS model with m-array formulation with missing visits

messages.author: 39971e2c19b8ec70
messages.subject: CJS model with m-array formulation with missing visits
parts:
Hi guys,

Is it possible to fit the Cormack-Jolly-Seber model with the m-array formulation (described e.g. in the BPA book from Marc & Michael) in case of missing visits/occasions (i.e. with NAs in the observations)? It is easily possible with capture histories, but it seems that with m-arrays NA would be taken as zero which is not good. Did you find solution for this or did you just use individual capture histories?

Tomas

PS: perhaps the workaround could be to make a specific m-array row for each pattern of NAs in the data.. Or, specific m-array for each site. Would you use this solution or is there something simpler?

messages.author: 0216939e087e502c
messages.subject: Re: CJS model with m-array formulation with missing visits
parts:
Dear Tomas,


if there are missing values for some occasions for all individuals simultaneously, then it appears to me that this is quite easy: you simply set to zero the recapture probability for those occasions.


If on the other hand the missing-value pattern is individual-specific, then it would become a little more involved for the m-array formulation of the model. But I find it hard to envision a sampling situation that would produce such data.


Best regards  --- Marc

messages.subject: Re: CJS model with m-array formulation with missing visits
parts:
Hi Marc,

it is the second case, and the situation is actually very common - Constant Effort Sites ringing programme. Not all sites have been monitored in all years, hence missing visits/occasions. Almost every country has data like that and I would be surprised if they have all visits on all sites.

Any simple m-array solution for that, except the complicated one I sketched?

Thanks and best regards,

Tomas

messages.author: 312eda23f89ab6c6
messages.subject: AW: CJS model with m-array formulation with missing visits
parts:
Hi Tomas,

I think that there is no "m-array solution" for this problem in the sense that you could have missing values somewhere in the data table. Rather as Marc has pointed out, you set in the CJS model the recapture probability to zero at the occasions without capture. Since the pattern of missing years is site specific, you would need to construct an m-array for each site and then fix the recapture to zero in a site-specific way in your model.

Kind regards

Michael
